summary: This is a clipped Hong Kong Observatory page for its 9-day weather forecast, mostly navigation and template placeholders with few concrete values. The substantive content is an explanatory note: the 50% range definitions based on 1991-2020 climate data, the Probability of Significant Rain (PSR) categories, and statements on how forecast accuracy declines with lead time and varies by season and weather system.
one_line: Hong Kong Observatory explainer on how its 9-day forecast, temperature/humidity ranges, and Probability of Significant Rain categories work.
key_facts: The 9-day Weather Forecast for Hong Kong is published by the Hong Kong Observatory (HKO) and provides general indications of weather trends for the coming 9 days.

The middle 50% range (between 25th and 75th percentiles) is calculated from maximum/minimum temperature and relative humidity data within a 5-day period centred on that day in the 30 years from 1991 to 2020.
For detailed description of today's weather forecast, users are referred to the "Local Weather Forecast".
The Probability of Significant Rain (PSR) forecast indicates the probability of accumulated rainfall generally over Hong Kong reaching 10 mm or more on a given day.
10 mm is described as around the mean daily rainfall in the rainy season.
The PSR category "High" is defined as 70% or above.
The PSR category "Medium High" is defined as 55-69%.
The PSR category "Medium" is defined as 45-54%.
The PSR category "Medium Low" is defined as 30-44%.
The PSR category "Low" is defined as less than 30%.
Average forecast accuracy for the next one to three days, four to seven days, and eight to nine days is about 90%, 85% and 80% respectively, for elements other than PSR.
PSR forecast errors in the next one to six days are within around 10%, and within around 20% for seven to nine days.
Forecast accuracy generally decreases and error generally increases with forecast period.
Weather in spring and summer, such as fog, tropical cyclones and severe convective weather, is more changeable, resulting in higher forecast uncertainty.
